Hi Elena — great questions, and absolutely doable. Below is a concise implementation plan we typically use to balance latency and unit cost during onboarding. I attached our checklist and a short recommendation doc for quant profiles.

Summary plan (high level):
1) Discovery & baseline (2 business days)
   - Run baseline traces on representative requests (single-turn and multi-turn) to measure p50/p95, tokens/sec, KV cache hit rates.
   - Deliverable: baseline_latency_report.pdf (attached)

2) Config experiments (3-5 business days)
   - Batching: start with conservative batch sizes (batch window 10-30ms), measure tail latency; increment batch size to find knee where cost drops with acceptable p95 impact. Expected outcome: 20-40% token-cost reduction for non-interactive batch jobs.
   - Caching: enable prefix/KV caching for repeatable system prompts and first-turn prefixes; expect 15-30% token savings for chat-heavy flows. Implementation requires lightweight client-side cache keys and server-side KV enablement.
   - Quantization profile selection: run evals across nf4 and int8 profiles (we've seen nf4 give near fp16 quality/1.8x speed, int8 gives bigger cost wins but needs evals). Recommendation: canary nf4 first, then measure quality delta against your eval set.

3) Routing & fallbacks (1-2 business days)
   - Define routing policy: prefer regional low-cost pool for background/embedding workloads; route interactive customer-facing traffic to lowest-latency pool (SLA-backed) with automatic fallback to compatible quantized variant on saturation.

4) Rollout & monitoring (ongoing)
   - Canary rollout (5-10% traffic) with automated quality/regression checks via Redwood Optimize prompt sets.
   - Observability: token-level cost, per-model latency, and cache hit metrics instrumented in Console.

Estimated owners:
- Redwood onboarding lead: Marissa Cole — overall project owner and runbook owner.
- Redwood infra/ops: Dev Patel — will own quant profile bench, kernel selection, and Dedicated config.
- Customer: Elena + one engineer (for test harness and eval data).

Costs: with expected batching + caching + nf4 quantization, customers frequently see 30-60% lower per-token inference cost vs baseline fp16 serving. We'll include specific projections after the baseline run.

Proposed kickoff: Thu May 21 09:00-10:00 PT (30m) — will bring the onboarding checklist and test harness instructions.

Attachments: rw_implementation_checklist.xlsx, baseline_latency_report.pdf, quant_profiles_recommendation.md

Let me know if you want us to include procurement directly on the kickoff.

Best,
Connor O'Brien

On Wed, May 13, 2026 at 10:21 AM Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com> wrote:
> Hi Elena — great questions, and absolutely doable. Below is a concise implementation plan we typically use to balance latency and unit cost during onboarding. I attached our checklist and a short recommendation doc for quant profiles.

Implementation checklist (detailed):
- Pre-kickoff: share 2 weeks of representative API traces + example prompts (customer responsibility).
- Baseline run: Redwood will run a 24h baseline on hosted variant and produce per-endpoint p50/p95 + token counts.
- Batching experiment plan: list of non-interactive endpoints to fold into batch windows, expected batch window sizes.
- KV caching plan: keys to cache (system prompts, onboarding prefixes), TTLs, and cache invalidation strategy.
- Quantization eval plan: evaluation dataset, quality gates (ROUGE/BLEU or human pass/fail), target thresholds.
- Routing policy draft: cost vs latency priority mapping by route and region.
- Success criteria: p95 < 220ms for interactive flow AND <40% increase in error/quality regressions post-quantization.

I suggest we also identify whether Dedicated capacity is preferred up front. If you need predictable throughput for batch jobs, Dedicated with reserved GPU pools simplifies routing and gives us control over autoscaling/burst policies.

Action items before kickoff (owner / ETA):
- FinTechCo: share traces + eval set (Elena) — due Tue May 19 EOD.
- Redwood: baseline run and initial quant recommendations (Dev) — due Wed May 20 EOD.
- Procurement: initial SOW template and estimated monthly committed spend (Connor) — due Wed May 20.

I'll prepare the runbook and a short demo of the Console dashboards we will use for monitoring.

Marissa Cole
